criteria.no: The item does not state the directive: it is silent about it, names only the topic, or describes a different approach.
criteria.unclear: The item states part of the directive's content but it cannot be determined whether it plans the directive itself.
criteria.yes: The item says that on a sanity FAIL the checked bead is reopened to its assignee and the dev is sent the sanity-fail.xml.j2 message on the open task.

addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires that on a sanity FAIL below the round cap the sanity close hook reopens the checked bead to its assignee and sends that dev the sanity-fail.xml.j2 template naming each undone deliverable on the dev's still-open task, creating no finding bead, new layer or new task. Does `item.text` state this directive's specific content as a step, constraint or decision? An item that only names the topic, or that creates finding beads, a new layer or a new task instead, does not state it. Judge presence of the directive only, not whether the item conflicts with it.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item is one of the ruled-out cases, including when the item is silent about the directive.
criteria.unclear: The item is ambiguous enough that it might describe one of the ruled-out cases, but it cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: The item states a plan, approach or decision that is one of the ruled-out cases.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan something that `anchor.statement` rules out? The anchor rules out: creating finding beads or child beads for a sanity FAIL; cutting a new layer or branch for the fix; creating or assigning a new ATM task for the fix; not reopening the checked bead on a FAIL that is below the round cap. These are not a conflict: silence about FAIL handling; escalating to the lead without reopening when a FAIL reaches max_sanity_rounds, because the statement covers only FAILs below the cap; incrementing the round counter. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system or a different activity, and completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell what part of the system it touches.
criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about, directly or as a clear prerequisite.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.

anchor.statement: On a sanity FAIL below the round cap, the sanity close hook must reopen the checked bead to its assignee and send that dev the sanity-fail.xml.j2 template naming each undone deliverable, on the dev's still-open task; it must not create finding beads, a new layer or a new task.
anchor.scope: atm-task-close.py sanity role on FAIL; templates/sanity-fail.xml.j2; retirement of sanity-create-findings and dev-fix.xml.j2

item.text: The sanity FAIL handling is redesigned in this sprint.
